close_reason: Resolved: the at_type shape divergence is spec-driven and intentional, not a cookie-cutter inconsistency. RFC 8984 marks every @type (mandatory) — 12 such annotations and zero defaultType in the spec — so jmap-jscalendar-types correctly uses bare 'at_type: String'. RFC 9553 §1.3.4 introduces the defaultType notation, which the workspace canonical-templates rule explicitly accommodates: 'differences mandated by the relevant RFC or draft' are permitted. The bead's hypothesis that RFC 8984 also has defaultType rules turned out to be wrong on inspection — no defaultType in RFC 8984. Documented the resolution in both crates' PLAN.md and AGENTS.md so future contributors don't try to harmonize the spec-driven difference. No code change. Tests pass (17 jscalendar + 58 jscontact).
description: Workspace AGENTS.md mandates cookie-cutter consistency: 'every type crate looks like every other type crate'. crate-jmap-jscalendar-types/src/lib.rs:123 et al. uses 'pub at_type: String' (mandatory, no Option, no default). crate-jmap-jscontact-types/src/lib.rs:95 et al. uses 'pub at_type: Option<String>' with default + skip_serializing_if. The jscontact choice is arguably more correct for RFC 9553 §1.3.4 defaultType-omission (and the AnniversaryDate.PartialDate-default test at lib.rs:1486 depends on it), but the divergence is undocumented. Future contributor (a) tries to harmonize by changing one to match the other and breaks the spec-driven behaviour, or (b) writes new types in one crate using the other's idiom. Resolution: pick one canonical shape for @type across both crates, document the decision (including the defaultType-omission story for RFC 8984 sub-types that have analogous defaults), and propagate. Most likely jscalendar-types should adopt the Option<String> shape since RFC 8984 also has defaultType rules.
title: at_type shape diverges from canonical sibling jmap-jscalendar-types
